turns.prompt: What is wisp and how do I use it?

blocks.title: Send agents off. Read the highlights.
blocks.summary: wisp launches coding agents in the background and hands you a short visual brief when they finish — not a transcript. Follow up right here.

items.title: Launch
items.detail: Press N, describe the task, pick the project folder. Launch several — they run in parallel.

items.title: Forget about it
items.detail: The queue on the left shows what each agent is doing in one line.

items.title: Review
items.detail: Finished work lands in “Needs you” with a dot. Open it to see the brief.

items.title: Follow up or close
items.detail: Reply to resume the same agent session, or press E to mark it done.

blocks.caption: Real diffs come from the agent’s own edits — no copy-paste.

items.note: Returns a presentation instead of the raw log.

before.label: Without wisp
items: Scroll 40 screens to find what changed
Lose track of which tab finished

after.label: With wisp
items: Fire and forget, many at once
A queue that tells you what needs you

blocks.command: npx wisp "add dark mode to the settings page"
blocks.output:
◌ wisp is floating at http://localhost:4477

  launched: add dark mode to the settings page

items.text: Edits — the agent may change files; anything else it needs, you approve
Full auto — no permission prompts at all; the default, each task in its own worktree

blocks.caption: Agents answer with blocks like these — you can ask for any of them.

blocks.title: Agents can ask you mid-run
blocks.text: When a decision matters, the agent pauses with a question. The session jumps to **Needs you**; your answer goes straight back to the still-running agent.

blocks.title: Heads up
blocks.text: This tour is static. Launch a real wisp with **N** — or take any real session over in your terminal with **T**.
